answer: Randomized Witness Assignment. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws a seed no one can predict beforehand, then assigns each agent a random set of witnesses to co-sign its actions, like scattered karst stones no attacker can map ahead. An identity that fails its assigned witness quorum is discarded, and because assignments shift unpredictably, an attacker must sustain a real, responsive vine of distinct live nodes per identity across every epoch. The atlas of required witnesses grows with each sybil, raising per-identity cost sharply.
